### Question 2a: Characteristic polynomial

```{r}
# https://edstem.org/au/courses/41412/lessons/119127/slides/817728
# Characteristic polynomial: See example example 0.12

Sigma <- matrix(c(6, 3,
                  3, 8), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)

print(Sigma)
cat("\n")

# Characteristic polynomial: lambda^2 - tr(Sigma)*lambda + det(Sigma)
tr  <- sum(diag(Sigma))
dt  <- det(Sigma)
cat("(a) lambda^2 -", tr, "* lambda +", dt, "\n")

```

### Question 2b: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors

```{r}
# https://edstem.org/au/courses/41412/lessons/119127/slides/817728
# See example 0.12 for R code

# Eigenvalues and #Eigenvectors
eigen <- eigen(Sigma)
lambda <- eigen$values     # eigen() returns eigenvalues in decreasing order
evectors <- eigen$vectors  # columns are normalised eigenvectors

print("Eigenvalues")
print(round(lambda, 4))
cat("\n")
print("Eigenvectors")
print(round(evectors, 4))

```

### Question 2c: Sigma^(1/2)

```{r}
# https://edstem.org/au/courses/41412/lessons/119127/slides/817728
# See equation (0.8), X = PΛPᵀ, where P holds the orthonormal eigenvectors
# Use windows Characters Map and open the app. Check the "Advanced view" box, search for modifier letter capital t, click Select, and then Copy.
# equation (0.10) defines sigma^(1/2) using sqrt(lambda)

# Sigma^(1/2) = P diag(sqrt(lambda)) Pᵀ
Sigma_half <- evectors %*% diag(sqrt(lambda)) %*% t(evectors)
print(round(Sigma_half, 4))

```

### Question 2d: Sigma^(-1/2)

```{r}

# (d) Sigma^(-1/2) = P diag(1/sqrt(lambda)) Pᵀ
Sigma_neghalf <- evectors %*% diag(1 / sqrt(lambda)) %*% t(evectors)
print(round(Sigma_neghalf, 4))
cat("\n")

# Checks
print("Checks")
round(Sigma_half %*% Sigma_half, 6)                  # this should equal Sigma
round(Sigma_neghalf %*% Sigma %*% Sigma_neghalf, 6)  # this should equal identity

```
